data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for general facts.

answers.answer: If you heat water, it boils.
If you will heat water, it boils.
If you heated water, it will boil.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: First conditional for real future possibilities.
sections.explain: Structure: If + present simple, will + base verb.

answers.answer: If I pass the exam, I will apply for the job.
If I will pass the exam, I apply for the job.
If I passed the exam, I will apply for the job.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Second conditional uses past simple + would + base verb.

answers.answer: If I had more time, I would travel more.
If I have more time, I would travel more.
If I would have more time, I travel more.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: First conditional with clause order variation.
sections.explain: Main clause can come first: will + verb + if + present simple.

answers.answer: We will miss the train if we leave late.
We will miss the train if we will leave late.
We would miss the train if we leave late.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: Use past simple after 'if' even for present unreal situations.

answers.answer: If she knew the answer, she would tell us.
If she knows the answer, she would tell us.
If she would know the answer, she tells us.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: 'When' is used instead of 'if' for events that are certain.

answers.answer: When I arrive, I will call you.
When I will arrive, I call you.
When I arrived, I will call you.
If I were you, I would accept the offer.
If I was you, I will accept the offer.
If I am you, I would accept the offer.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.explain: First conditional can use modals like 'might' instead of 'will'.

answers.answer: If it rains, we might stay home.
If it will rain, we might stay home.
If it rained, we might stayed home.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Zero conditional for rules and instructions.
sections.explain: Zero conditional is used for instructions and general rules.

answers.answer: If you press this button, the machine starts.
If you will press this button, the machine starts.
If you pressed this button, the machine starts.

sections.question: Choose the correct sentence.
sections.summary: Contrast between first and second conditional.
sections.explain: Use first conditional for real future; second conditional for unreal situations.

answers.answer: If she studies hard, she will pass; if she studied harder, she would get a scholarship.
If she studies hard, she would pass; if she studied harder, she will get a scholarship.
If she will study hard, she will pass; if she studied harder, she would get a scholarship.
